text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on September 14 in history.

1321 - Dante, full name Dante Alighieri, Italy's greatest poet, died. He was also a prose writer, literary theorist, moral philosopher and political thinker. His Christian epic "The Divine Comedy" is regarded as one of the landmarks of world literature.
1515 - Francis I of France defeated the Swiss at the Battle of Marignano, resulting in the French recovery of Milan.
1741 - The German-born English composer George Frederick Handel finished his "Messiah" oratorio, after working on it non-stop for 23 days.

1752 - Britain and its colonies adopted the Gregorian calendar. The error which had built up in the Julian calendar over the centuries was rectified by eliminating 11 days. Parliament decreed that the day after September 2 would be September 14. Thus in British and American history there are no references to September 3-13, 1752.
1812 - Napoleon entered Moscow in his disastrous invasion of Russia. The city was set on fire by the retreating Russians and burned until September 19, destroying much of the capital.
1814 - Francis Scott Key wrote "The Star-Spangled Banner", which, in 1931, became the U.S. national anthem.
1851 - James Fenimore Cooper, U.S. novelist famous for his novels of frontier adventure, including "The Last of the Mohicans", died.

1852 - The Duke of Wellington (Arthur Wellesley) died. Noted as a military commander, his biggest achievement was the defeat of Napoleon at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815. He was British prime minister 1828-30.
1868 - Golf's first recorded hole-in-one was scored by Scotsman Tom Morris at Prestwick's 166-yard 8th hole, during the Open Championships.
1901 - U.S. President William McKinley died from his wounds after an assassination attempt on September 6. He was succeeded in office by Theodore Roosevelt.
1927 - Isadora Duncan, U.S. ballet dancer, was killed in a motor accident in Nice, France. She was strangled by a long scarf that became caught in the wheel of a car in which she was riding.
1930 - In Germany, in a stunning election triumph, the National Socialist (Nazi) Party became the second largest party in the Reichstag (parliament).
1937 - Thomas Masaryk, Czech revolutionary leader who in 1918 became the country's first president, died.
1959 - The Soviet Union's Luna-2 became the first spacecraft to land on the Moon.
1974 - Giant pandas Chia Chia and Ching Ching, a gift from China to British Prime Minister Edward Heath when he visited there in 1973, arrived in London.
1975 - In Amsterdam, Rembrandt's priceless painting "The Nightwatch" was slashed by an unemployed teacher with a kitchen knife.

1982 - Princess Grace of Monaco, formerly American film actress Grace Kelly, who appeared in films such as "High Noon", "Dial M for Murder" and "High Society", died in hospital after a car crash the previous day.
1982 - Lebanese president-elect Bashir Gemayel was assassinated in a bomb explosion at his party headquarters in East Beirut.

1994 - Israeli Foreign Minister Shimon Peres and Palestine Liberation Organisation Chairman Yasser Arafat signed a declaration aimed at unblocking $2.5 billion of aid for Palestinian self-rule territories.
